This text is from Book 19 (lines 184–197) of Homer's ***Iliad***. It is the moment when King Agamemnon responds to Odysseus, agreeing to formally reconcile with Achilles, bring him gifts, and swear an oath that he never touched Achilles' war-prize, Briseis. 

Here is the English translation:

Then Agamemnon, king of men, answered him [Odysseus]:
"Son of Laertes, I rejoice to hear these words from you,
for you have gone through and recounted everything just as is proper.
I am willing to swear this oath, and my heart urges me to do so,
and I shall not swear falsely before the god. But let Achilles
remain here for a time, even though he is eager for war;
and let all the rest of you remain gathered together, until the gifts
are brought from my tent and we seal our binding oaths.
And to you yourself, I give this order and command:
Choose the best young men of all the Achaeans,
and bring from my ship all the gifts that we promised yesterday
to give to Achilles, and fetch the women as well.
And let Talthybius swiftly make his way through the broad camp of the Achaeans
and prepare a boar for me to sacrifice to Zeus and the Sun."

***

**A few notes on the translation from the ancient Greek text:**
* **Line 185 (Λαερτιάδη):** Addresses Odysseus by his patronymic, "Son of Laertes." 
* **Line 191 (ὅρκια πιστὰ τάμωμεν):** Literally translates to "cut trustworthy oaths." In ancient Greece, oaths were sworn by cutting the throats of sacrificial animals, hence the idiom.
* **Line 196 (Ταλθύβιος):** Talthybius was Agamemnon's herald and messenger. 
* **Line 197 (Διί τ᾽ Ἠελίῳ τε):** Agamemnon is ordering a sacrifice to Zeus (the highest god who oversees oaths) and Helios (the Sun, who sees everything from above, making him a traditional witness to oaths).

Translate this (ancient) Greek text to English:
τὸν δ᾽ αὖτε προσέειπεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων:
‘185χαίρω σεῦ Λαερτιάδη τὸν μῦθον ἀκούσας:
ἐν μοίρῃ γὰρ πάντα διίκεο καὶ κατέλεξας.
ταῦτα δ᾽ ἐγὼν ἐθέλω ὀμόσαι, κέλεται δέ με θυμός,
οὐδ᾽ ἐπιορκήσω πρὸς δαίμονος. αὐτὰρ Ἀχιλλεὺς
μιμνέτω αὐτόθι τεῖος ἐπειγόμενός περ Ἄρηος:
190μίμνετε δ᾽ ἄλλοι πάντες ἀολλέες, ὄφρά κε δῶρα
ἐκ κλισίης ἔλθῃσι καὶ ὅρκια πιστὰ τάμωμεν.
σοὶ δ᾽ αὐτῷ τόδ᾽ ἐγὼν ἐπιτέλλομαι ἠδὲ κελεύω:
κρινάμενος κούρητας ἀριστῆας Παναχαιῶν
δῶρα ἐμῆς παρὰ νηὸς ἐνεικέμεν, ὅσσ᾽ Ἀχιλῆϊ
195χθιζὸν ὑπέστημεν δώσειν, ἀγέμεν τε γυναῖκας.
Ταλθύβιος δέ μοι ὦκα κατὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν
κάπρον ἑτοιμασάτω ταμέειν Διί τ᾽ Ἠελίῳ τε.
